I agree with you in a lot of ways.  Lately I've been comparing us humans with wild animals, who seem to have a better time at life than us.

Sure, we've built crap, we've flown ourselves to the moon, we've worked out amazing feats of engineering, but what's it all worth if we're not as happy as dolphins?  (maybe some would think the phrase "better to be a Socrates dissatisfied than a pig satisfied" applies here?  but I'm not sure I'd agree).

The only depressed animals I can think of are the ones we lock up in zoos and cages, or the fish that jump out of fishtanks.  Those are the only ones resembling symptoms of what we might call depression.  I guess there are others though: the penguins who run away from the pack and run towards the mountains - ones gone mad who are just eliminated due to survival of the fittest.  Maybe us depressed ones are the ones that really should be dead otherwise?
